accepted.title: The dessert tent
accepted.text: At a family wedding reception, Abdul and Siddharth are restless. Siddharth points toward the closed catering area where trays of special sweets are being set up. "Let's sneak behind the curtain and grab some rasmalai before the counters open," Abdul whispers. "Come on, nobody is looking!" What do you do?

options.text: Sneak in with them so they don't tease me for backing out
options.consequence: A caterer catches you all by the dessert table and firmly asks you to leave.

options.text: Tell them firmly, "No, sneaking into the kitchen is wrong and against the rules."
options.consequence: Siddharth sighs, but both boys drop the idea and stay out of the tent.

options.text: Say no, but suggest heading to the open juice counter instead
options.consequence: They agree that drinks sound fun, and you all grab juice without causing trouble.

hint.text: Can you stand your ground while helping your friends find something fun and safe to do?

grade.rationale: Option C demonstrates excellent relationship skills and decision-making by setting a clear boundary against rule-breaking while constructively redirecting peers. Option B is also a solid assertion of rules and limits. Option A succumbs to peer pressure out of fear of teasing, showing weak self-management and decision-making.

reasons: Culturally authentic scenario for Indian children at a family wedding.
Accurately maps to the research construct with realistic options and believable outcomes.

accepted.title: The shiny new bats
accepted.text: Coach places shiny new cricket bats on the bench. "Nobody touches these until warm-up is over," Coach says, then walks to the gate. Aarav nudges you. "Let's just hold one for a second!" You really want to try it. What do you do?

options.consequence: Coach turns around, spots you holding it, and asks you to sit out the first drill.

options.text: Move away to the pitch and do your stretches so you stop looking at them
options.consequence: Focusing on stretches makes the wait easier, and Coach calls everyone over soon.

options.text: Take a quick swing, then tell Coach as soon as he returns that you didn't wait
options.consequence: Coach reminds you about following team rules, but appreciates that you owned up.

hint.text: What can help take your mind off something you really want right now?

accepted.title: Shared slides
accepted.text: You were reviewing Mohit's presentation slides before sharing them in the class group chat. While editing on your phone, you accidentally deleted his two main summary slides and saved the file. In the chat, Mohit panics: "Did the link crash? My whole section is gone!" Nobody saw your edit. What do you do?

options.text: Message Mohit privately, admit you accidentally deleted it, and help him restore the version history
options.consequence: Mohit is relieved the work isn't permanently lost, and together you get the slides back.

options.text: Own up in the group chat right away and offer to retype his summary from scratch
options.consequence: Mohit appreciates your honesty, though he feels a bit stressed about the lost time.

options.text: Suggest in the chat that the app glitched and everyone should help him redo his notes
options.consequence: The group rushes to help, but Mohit stays anxious and you feel uneasy about not speaking up.

options.text: Stay silent so you don't look careless in front of the whole class
options.consequence: Mohit stays up late redoing his section, frustrated that his hard work vanished.

hint.text: What action actually helps Mohit get his work back fastest without adding to his panic?

grade.rationale: Admitting an accidental mistake privately and helping fix it demonstrates strong responsibility and relationship skills. Concealing the mistake or lying about a tech glitch prioritizes reputation over honesty and fairness.

accepted.title: Behind the Stage Curtains
accepted.text: At the annual day rehearsal, Manav hides behind the curtains. He has been very worried for days about speaking on stage, and he looks ready to cry. He whispers, 'Please do not tell anyone.' What do you do?

options.text: Tell him to just laugh it off and be brave
options.consequence: Manav curls up tighter behind the curtain, feeling misunderstood.

options.text: Promise to keep his secret and go back to practice
options.consequence: Manav stays hidden alone in the dark, still deeply worried.

options.text: Gently offer to walk with him to talk to the teacher
options.consequence: The teacher listens softly and finds a backstage role where Manav feels safe.

hint.text: Who can help when a worry is too big to handle alone?

grade.rationale: Option C offers gentle support while helping Manav address his severe stage fright with a trusted adult. Dismissing his feelings (Option A) or leaving him alone in secret distress (Option B) are unhelpful. Balancing a friend's request for secrecy with their need for assistance is a realistic dilemma for children aged 8–10.

Skillfully addresses the dilemma between keeping a friend's secret and seeking help from a trusted adult when distress is overwhelming.
Consequences are natural, empathetic, and avoid clinical labels or preachiness.

feelingsStayReal.note: Manav's overwhelming worry is acknowledged without dismissing it as trivial.

accepted.title: The upstairs room
accepted.text: At Joseph's birthday party, Sneha urges everyone to sneak upstairs to his brother's room to use the gaming console. "His parents are busy downstairs, they won't even notice," Sneha whispers. Joseph looks uneasy because his parents strictly told guests not to go upstairs, but he is hesitant to disagree with Sneha. The others turn to you to decide. What do you do?

options.text: Head upstairs with Sneha so the group doesn't leave you out
options.consequence: Joseph's brother discovers everyone minutes later, and the party atmosphere becomes uncomfortable.

options.text: Say a firm no and explain that you won't break Joseph's house rules
options.consequence: Sneha rolls her eyes at you, but Joseph looks visibly relieved that someone spoke up.

options.text: Suggest setting up a multiplayer round on your phones downstairs instead
options.consequence: Sneha grumbles at first, but the whole group soon gathers around the living room table to play.

options.text: Quietly tell Joseph's mother that Sneha wants to go upstairs
options.consequence: She gently reminds everyone to stay downstairs, though Sneha realises you told on her and walks away.

hint.text: How can you keep the party fun without putting Joseph in a difficult position?

grade.rationale: Option C offers a constructive, inclusive alternative that respects house rules while keeping the party fun. accepted.title: The last cricket bat

options.text: Yank the bat away and claim you touched it first

options.consequence: Arnav bats with others, while you spend recess feeling disappointed.

accepted.title: Secret at the market
accepted.text: At the busy market with Papa, you spot your friend Lakshmi looking upset near a stall. Lakshmi whispers that an older kid on her street has been blocking her way home every day and scaring her. She begs you not to tell any grown-up. What do you do?

options.consequence: Lakshmi feels nervous, but Papa listens calmly and offers to speak with her parents.

options.text: Promise to keep her secret and offer to walk with her tomorrow

options.consequence: Papa thanks you for sharing a safety worry and calls Lakshmi's family to support them.

options.text: Tell Lakshmi to just ignore the kid so nobody gets into trouble

accepted.title: Festival coins in the chat

accepted.title: Roasted Chana at the Market
accepted.text: While my mother bargains for vegetables across the crowded market lane, I run into Anjali and Esha. Anjali points to a busy cart vendor whose back is turned. options.text: Laugh and grab a handful with them so they don't call me boring

options.text: Say a firm no: "No, that's taking his food without paying."
options.consequence: Anjali rolls her eyes at you, but both of them keep their hands in their pockets.

options.text: Say no, and suggest we pool our pocket change to buy a cone together
options.consequence: Esha checks her pockets, and the three of you pitch in ten rupees to share a warm bag.

options.text: Walk straight back to my mother without answering
options.consequence: You stay out of trouble, though you keep looking over your shoulder to see what they will do.

hint.text: How can you stand your ground without losing your friends?

grade.rationale: This scenario tests a child's ability to resist peer pressure and act honestly. Option C shows excellent relationship skills and responsible decision-making by turning a dishonest idea into a positive, cooperative solution. Option A succumbs to pressure and promotes stealing.

options.text: Own up to Farhan, apologise to both of them, and offer your trip pocket money toward a replacement
options.consequence: Farhan is upset about the earbud, but he clears Shreya's name and agrees to figure out the cost.

options.text: Suggest to Farhan that the bus floor was crowded and anyone could have trampled it accidentally
options.consequence: Farhan stays frustrated with everyone around him, and Shreya remains quiet and hurt.

options.text: Say nothing now, but quietly slip your own spare earphones into Farhan's bag later
options.consequence: Farhan accepts the spare, but Shreya remains deeply hurt that nobody believed her.

hint.text: What does Shreya need in this moment, and what would genuinely set things right with Farhan?

grade.rationale: Owning up when an innocent person is blamed requires courage, honesty, and fair restitution. Option B clearly shows responsible decision-making and relationship skills by clearing Shreya and offering to pay for the damage. The other options avoid direct accountability and leave a classmate in distress.

reasons: Accurately reflects the construct of owning up to an unseen mistake when another person is falsely blamed.
Consequences are realistic: Farhan remains upset while appreciating the honesty, avoiding magical fixes.
Maintains respectful, age-appropriate language and culturally relatable context.

honestConsequences.note: Consequences realistically balance Farhan's understandable frustration with the relief of resolving the unfair blame.

feelingsStayReal.note: Farhan's upset feelings and Shreya's distress are acknowledged rather than bypassed or minimized.

showNotPreach.note: Outcomes show the relational ripple effects directly without moralising or adult lectures.

certaintyFits.note: In a scenario where an innocent peer is accused of one's own mistake, truthfulness and restitution is unambiguously the right course.

noShaming.note: Options and consequences describe believable avoidance behaviours neutrally without calling the player names.

notATherapist.note: Free of clinical language or therapeutic overreach.

realForIndianChildren.note: School bus trips, borrowed gadgets, and trip pocket money are very natural touchstones for Indian middle schoolers.

candidate.title: The Bent Nib
candidate.text: On the bumpy school bus ride home, you borrow Chirag's new fountain pen to finish your revision sheet. When the bus swerves, the nib catches on your bag's buckle and bends completely out of shape. Chirag is laughing two rows ahead with Aarav and didn't see what happened. What do you do?

options.text: Slide the pen back into his open pouch quietly and look out the window
options.consequence: Chirag finds the damaged nib later, wondering aloud who stepped on his bag.

options.text: Walk over right now, show him the bent nib, and offer to buy a replacement from your allowance
options.consequence: Chirag looks upset about the pen, but he agrees to check the stationery shop together tomorrow.

options.text: Wait until you reach his bus stop so you can tell him privately without everyone watching
options.consequence: You spend the ride worrying, but Chirag listens calmly when you explain at the stop.

options.text: Hand it back and say the bus driver's rash driving caused it to break
options.consequence: Chirag takes the pen with a frown, unconvinced and quiet for the rest of the journey.

hint.text: What would help Chirag still trust you after an accident like this?

grade.rationale: This scenario presents a realistic dilemma for 11-14 year olds involving accidents, ownership, and social pressure. Options B and C both show honesty, but C demonstrates extra social awareness by choosing a private setting to handle an uncomfortable situation thoughtfully without creating an unnecessary public scene.

reasons: Off-category: aimed at responsibleDecisionMaking (1), but the grader found the best option mainly shows socialAwareness (2), relationshipSkills (2)

candidate.title: The Fort Steps
candidate.text: On a school trip, Harsh walks slowly up the steep fort steps because of his leg brace. A few classmates giggle and run ahead, leaving him far behind. Harsh stops and looks down quietly. What do you do?

options.text: Run ahead with the fast group so I don't miss out
options.consequence: You reach the top quickly, but Harsh is left far behind on the stairs.

options.text: Walk at Harsh's pace and look at the old walls together
options.consequence: Harsh smiles, and neither of you feels rushed on the climb.

options.text: Call out gently, "Hey, let's all walk together!"
options.consequence: Two classmates slow down and wait on the steps for Harsh.

options.text: Tell our teacher that Harsh is being left behind
options.consequence: The teacher stops the line so the whole class stays together.

hint.text: How might Harsh feel climbing those big steps alone?

grade.rationale: This scenario presents a clear opportunity for empathy and inclusion when a peer with physical challenges is left behind. Options B and C demonstrate strong social awareness and relationship skills by supporting a peer and advocating for group inclusion, while Option A reflects peer pressure at the expense of kindness.

reasons: Off-category: aimed at responsibleDecisionMaking (1), but the grader found the best option mainly shows socialAwareness (2), relationshipSkills (2)

candidate.title: Whispers by the Bookshelf
candidate.text: In the library, Noor struggles to read Hindi words aloud for a group project. Vikram giggles and whispers, 'Don't let her read, she talks funny.' Noor looks down, clutching her book. What do you do?

options.text: Laugh along with Vikram so things don't get awkward
options.consequence: Vikram grins, but Noor pulls her chair away and stays completely silent.

options.text: Ask Noor if she wants to read the next sentence together with me
options.consequence: Noor looks up, nods shyly, and you both take turns on the page.

options.text: Tell Vikram calmly that making fun of her isn't fair
options.consequence: Vikram stops whispering and looks down, and Noor sits up a little straighter.

options.text: Go over and quietly tell the librarian what is happening
options.consequence: The librarian walks over to remind the group to be respectful, and Vikram stays quiet.

hint.text: How might Noor feel hearing those whispers?

grade.rationale: This scenario addresses peer pressure and exclusion. Laughing along is a tempting way to avoid awkwardness, but supporting a classmate or standing up for fairness is clearly the pro-social choice.
